native_source_families.meaning: two-state update on a record: state 0 marks a byte with 255 and either runs a shared two-call teardown when a global latch byte is set and a sub-object field is non-zero, or plays a mode/value pair plus a call; state 1 runs a setup call and two float queries against a stored table and, when both are below 2.0, plays three fixed calls and either tears down or writes 120 into a sub-object field
Decomposes a float returned by a bound producer into hours, minutes and hundredths written through three pointer arguments, rounding each step with a bound helper and clamping the last field at 99.

Picks one of two pointers held at +88 and +92 of the receiver, choosing +92 when the byte at +66 equals 255, then returns a value derived from the scale word at +68: either a halved table lookup, or a weighted blend of two table lookups plus the scale, or an interpolation between a lookup at +92 and a lookup at +88 weighted by one minus the scale.

Copies a 16-byte block pointed to by the first argument into a stack buffer, stores the three float arguments into a 16-byte stack vector, fills two 64-byte matrices through helper routines, applies copies of the buffer through them into two more 16-byte stack vectors, and finishes by passing the destination, the source and a composed vector to a closing routine.

Dispatches on one byte of a fixed global table: when it is zero it copies a 16-byte block from the second argument to the first and then accumulates two table-derived floats, each scaled by the third argument, into the first two words of that block; when it is 1 or 2 it builds a 16-byte vector from two table-derived values and a zero, fills two 64-byte matrices through helper routines, composes them into a vector and passes that vector with the two pointers to a closing routine.

Reads a float through a pointer field; returns when it is zero or when a word field is zero, otherwise calls a helper, adjusts a float loaded from another pointer field by half or all of the helper's result depending on a small mode word, and finally calls a second helper with three pointers and three floats taken from the object and from two further pointer fields.
looks up an object, then sets flags, arms a stored value and calls one of two helper pairs before building a timer

Calls a callee with the constant 167 and, when it returns a non-zero object, stores the argument pointer at +4 of the object held at +104, clears the words at +0, +8 and +12 of that object, sets byte +48 to 255, the halfword at +50 to 126 and bytes +49 and +32 to 0, then returns the object.
Reads the short at +26 of the object held at +104, calls a callee with (3076, that short), then calls one callee with this when the result is zero or three callees with this when it is non-zero.

Calls a callee on (second pointer, first pointer + 16); if the result is not below the first float argument it returns 0, otherwise it evaluates a second callee on (a float at second+8 minus a float at first+24) and returns 1 when that is below the second float argument, else 0.
Calls one callee with the argument 1, then a second callee with (first, second, third argument) keeping its result, calls the first callee again with 1, and returns the kept result.
initialises eight in-place sub-records of one object by four routines, then returns the object pointer
decrements a signed short counter and, at zero, rotates a 24-bit identifier beside it and reloads the counter; calls a helper when the identifier's top byte is clear
initialises eight in-place sub-records of one object by four routines, then returns the object pointer
stores a value into one field and, when a second field is set, clears it and calls the same callee with a zero argument on four sub-objects at a 148-byte stride
clamps a caller-supplied terminator value (-1 meaning unset) to 360, then runs two callees on two sub-objects of one handle, the second with a float pair
clamps a caller-supplied terminator value (-1 meaning unset) to 180, then runs two callees on two sub-objects of one handle, the second with a float pair
runs a fixed sequence of seven callees on one object handle, passing the address of two stack floats to the third callee and then their values to the fourth
returns 1 when a global state word is 49 and a global mode word is 4 or 11, otherwise 0; a callee returning nonzero short-circuits the result to 0

Compares the second argument with the word at offset 4 of the object; when they differ, and when the word at offset 44 is non-zero while the word at offset 24 is zero, it calls a two-argument helper with those two words, marks offset 24 with 1, and finally writes the second argument into offset 4.
Initialises eight sub-objects at byte offsets 8, 84, 160, 236 (step 76) and 312, 384, 456, 528 (step 72) of the argument with two different helpers and returns the argument.

Returns zero when a helper reports non-zero, otherwise combines three fields of the pointed-to block (a difference plus a third term, taken modulo that third term) scaled by a constant and added to the first field.

Halves the float argument and calls one helper with it, forwards the second and first arguments plus that helper result to a second helper, and stores a third helper result into the field at offset 12 of the first argument.
stores the count in a field, then loops count times calling one helper on each successive 72-byte slot and passing the result to a second helper.
loops 56 times calling a two-argument helper and, unless the current index is zero, a second one-argument helper with that index.
early-returns when a 32-bit field is zero, otherwise calls one helper four times and another three times with fixed byte offsets off the argument pointer.
branches on a pointer argument: when it is null, fills a 64-byte stack buffer from the object and calls a helper with the buffer, otherwise calls the same helper with that pointer.

On a byte-addressable root base: if the word at +6228 is set, calls a helper with it and clears it, then clears bits 0 and 6 of the 16-bit field at +52 of each object pointed to by the base words at +4880 and +4884.

Two-branch draw set-up: copies a 2-byte record from one of two tables into a 16-byte local, then issues a draw call with five float arguments (scale, per-instance angle, two constants, colour value) plus a 64-bit attribute word, a geometry handle, a fifth integer argument -1 and a local buffer.
Calls one callee with 1 and a second with no argument, then tests an absolute global word: when it is set it calls a callee with (512, 416, 640, 448, 0, 0), otherwise (512, 416, 512, 448, 0, 0).
Reads a bound global word; when it is zero it returns its first argument, otherwise it calls a helper with that value plus a fixed base offset and both of its arguments.
Reads a bound global word; when it is non-zero it calls a helper with that value plus a fixed base offset as the first argument and the function's own argument as the second, otherwise returns 0.

scans a 48-entry table of 20-byte records for a record whose first word equals an argument, and when the scan succeeds stores the found index into a short counter and calls a helper with (index, -1, second argument, 1).

Calls one routine twice with two different ids and a two-int scratch area, short-circuiting to a zero result if either fails, and otherwise returns whether a third routine's difference of the two ints is below a fourth incoming integer.

Initialises a 96-byte stack workspace, calls one routine on its first window with two of the incoming integers, fills the third window from a second routine, combines the three windows with a third routine, and returns one float of the middle window indexed by the fourth integer.

Walks a five-element array of 76-byte records starting at +12 of the argument, calling one routine on each record, then calls the same second routine on three fixed offsets (+408, +480, +552) and returns the argument.
Copies a 36-byte global record onto the stack, substitutes a default id when the argument is zero, and calls one helper with the id, the count 9 and two fixed global addresses.
Guards three fields of a level state block, calls one helper with two stack outputs, then copies a shared float into offset 72 of two optional objects.
reads a mode byte from a global block; when zero it forwards the arguments to one helper, otherwise it range-checks the byte and drives two helpers with the object and block pointers
scales a float field by 1/1024, stores an int argument in a stack record, and drives four helper calls with frame and object-field pointers

blends two table entries by the fractional part of a clock value: the integer part is the index, one step back is wrapped over a count unless a flag selects the last slot, and the result is frac*table[index] + (scale-frac)*table[previous]

Computes the x/y difference between one 16-byte record of the second handle and the record after the first handle's base, dispatches through three helpers and walks a short counter field up or down by one when the last helper's float result stays under a stored threshold.
clamps a float read through a pointer to plus/minus the second float argument, passes it through two helpers and stores the result back
scales a float argument by a field of the object into a stack buffer, then calls a second routine with the object, its flags, the buffer and three float arguments
unlinks a node from a singly linked list (head case and inner-chain case) and calls a release routine on it; does nothing for a null node
resets a sub-object, applies a two-float transform, and when bit 6 of flags is set and an int field is zero calls a mode setter and toggles a global byte
reads two object fields, forms centre plus and minus half of a third, and issues two five-argument draw calls taking an id-derived value and a fixed 64-bit attribute

dispatches on one byte of a global table with a three-case switch: case 0 scales two floats of the destination by the incoming scale, cases 1 and 2 first run a helper over the destination with a table at +64, scale the same two floats and then run a second helper with the destination as both source and destination

Bumps a 16-bit counter in a fixed data block and, when the new value exceeds the caller's threshold, builds a three-float jittered position from two globals plus three random calls, hands it to a spawn helper and stores the helper's return value back into the counter.
Scales two owner words by sampled unit-vector factors derived from two float inputs, then normalises each input in place.
Builds three vectors from an owner block, blends the stored value toward the closest of the sampled vector length and the stored reference gap, and writes the remaining gap back.

reads a pointer from the field at +112 of the first argument, advances it by 176, then runs three 16-byte records and two float parameters through a fixed sequence of seven calls that alternate between three helpers
queries a resident table with a stack request and blends a vector back into the resident record
shared native family
Derives a value from half of one argument, merges a helper's low byte into a packed word, then scales an input float, doubles a second helper's result and dispatches a seven-argument spawn.

Appends a record to a fixed four-entry table: aborts when the table is full or an index argument is out of range, copies selected fields from one linked record into a helper-allocated record, then stores the three inputs and that record into four parallel tables and bumps the count.
Advances a stored float by a scaled helper result, then clamps it against a positive limit, then clamps it again with a second helper and finally rescales it through a third helper.
Computes two sub-record addresses of a 192-byte block and hands three of its sub-records to four helpers, threading a second argument through two of them.

If a probe call on a sub-object returns zero, folds a byte counter into the top byte of a packed word, rebuilds a 16-byte vector from two sub-records for a helper, then clamps a running float against a limit and accumulates two sub-record fields into the object.

Copies 64 bytes of a source record onto the stack, normalises the last element of the copy to 1.0, queries three pairwise float angles from the copy after two scratch-matrix builds, and writes the three angles into the caller's output record.

Walks an inline array of element pointers; for each element whose sub-object flag at +4 is zero it rewrites a 270-degree angle to -90, scales it by pi/180, compares a helper result against 0.001 and routes it through one of two pi/2 helpers, toggles the flag, then calls a two-pointer helper with element+192 and element+240.

Updates a record: calls two helpers on the sub-object at +0x20 (float argument 0.975f), advances the float at +0x0C by 14700.0f, adds the byte at +0x30 into the byte at +0x08, then adds 0xFE000000 to the word at +0x04 and calls a third helper when the result is negative.

Initialises an object: runs setup helpers, clears word +0x4C, stores one helper result at +0x48, then calls a final helper with (small-data global + 0x3CAA8) only when two globals are non-zero, and returns 0.
Calls a callee with (this, word at +32), copies six words from +36..+56 down to +4..+24, calls the function pointer at +48 with this when non-zero, then clears +104.

Initialises an object: two float stores through the pointer at +0, clears byte +423, stores an int at +440, calls a callee with (this+168, -1) storing its result at +468 and the address at +472, sets +432 to 1 and writes 1.0f through the pointer at +4.
Stores an argument at +1012; if the word at +1024 is zero it returns, else it clears +1024, sets +12 to 1 and calls one callee four times on this+468/604/740/876 with argument 1.
Calls one float-conversion helper on (a0 %% a1) and again on a1, then returns 2*pi times the quotient minus pi.
dispatch on the second integer argument: each arm runs a pair of sub-calls passing the first argument twice, the second call also forwarding the float argument
reads a global mode value; for 8, 9 or 19 probes two engine queries and returns 1 if either reports true, else 0

Reads a word at +544 of the object; returns when it is zero, otherwise calls a repeated callee four times with the object and the objects at +152, +76 and +228, then one callee each with +464, the object, the object and the object.

Calls a callee with the object, returns when it fails, otherwise fills a 16-byte workspace from the object at +192 with 8.0f, hands it to a second callee through +96, calls a third, then stores 300 at +304.

Runs one helper over the object and a stack buffer, then builds a second call from the object's field 104 sub-object - its field 24 as a float, the constants 2.0f/5.0f/0.6f and a bound data address - and stores the object into field 184 of the returned pointer when it is non-null.
One-shot init: raises an int flag, forces a state word outside {6,7} to 5, runs three calls, then clears a 16-bit global.
Calls a routine on pointer-plus-10 and, when it returns non-zero, calls a second routine with the pointer itself.
Forwards one object pointer, eight pointer-plus-constant arguments and a null to ten calls in a fixed order.
walks four 76-byte records calling one function on each, then calls two more functions on later fields and returns its argument
If the linked global word is zero, stores (second_float_field - f) into the first object's float field; otherwise runs a three-call path over a 16-byte local buffer.
Blends a value toward a target: helper(second,first) halved, scaled by (1 - helper(third*pi)); the first argument and that product go to a two-float helper whose float result is returned.
builds one 64-byte block from a 3-float vector of the incoming scalars and another from a static table record one element in, combines them, then scales the result again from that record
stores a wrapped angle back into the caller field and forwards its [0,1] rescaled value (x*0.5+0.5) with two pointer arguments to a second callee
builds two 64-byte blocks from a 3-float vector and from a vector inside the caller object, combines them, then scales one block again from the same source vector
scales four 16-byte records of a static table in place by a scalar, then multiplies one float field of a later record by the same scalar
draws two bounded random angles and an interval random value from the two float arguments, then forwards the pointer, the interval draw and both angles to a fourth callee
Fills a three-float local through two setup calls, stores a two-argument float helper result into a field, then stores a second helper result into two more fields and returns zero.

Returns early when a float field reached through a two-level pointer chain is exactly zero; otherwise dispatches on an integer state (0 or 2 selects one of two callees) and then always calls a third callee with the same object pointer.
Loads a 32-bit global pointer from a fixed data address; if non-null, tail-forwards it (offset by 0x36F28) plus ten incoming arguments to an overlay-local callee.

Same body as 23626ad829daa908 with the node field 4 bytes earlier: calls a helper with a referenced node and three identity bytes, then copies them into a linked record guarded by a flag bit and a non-zero leading short.
Zeroes a 16-byte global block, calls a setup helper, runs a per-slot reset helper over seven 16-byte units of a global table, then clears three word fields of a block 256 bytes below the table base.

Stores the incoming handle into the record's first word and, for a non-negative index, into the next slot of a 112-byte-stride table, then either bumps a state short from 1 to 2 or passes three shorts and one word of a global block to a helper.

Calls a helper with a referenced node and three identity bytes of the object, then copies those bytes into a linked record when a node flag bit is set and the record exists with a non-zero leading short.
When a global flag is set, derives a pointer from that global plus a fixed offset, runs it through one callee and stores the callee result into a field of the argument.
Lazily initialises a sub-object of the argument behind two global flags and a field, runs one guarded setup step on it, then hands it to two callees.

Calls a one-argument helper three times with three fixed small integers, passes the three results and a pointer plus 8 to a four-argument helper, calls a two-argument helper with the same address and 0.0f, then clears the word at offset 764.
Adds the result of a two-argument helper, called three times with the same arguments, into each of three consecutive floats of a vector.

loads two object pointers from fixed data, bails out when either is null or when the first object's byte 67 differs from 1, fills two stack ints through a helper, then applies a four-argument operation to each object with those ints
runs a setup routine on a 16-byte stack buffer, selects 0.35f or 0.6f into buffer slot 2 from a flag byte in fixed data, then forwards the buffer with three float arguments
looks up three objects by numeric id, runs a four-argument routine and a (pointer,float) routine on a sub-object at self+8, then stores 1 at self+764
Calls twelve sub-object handlers in sequence, each with the object base plus a fixed byte offset (8, 684, 744, 816, 888, 960, 1040, 1112, 1184, 1256, 1328, 1400), then returns the object pointer.

Flag-gated record update: copies 16 bytes src->dst and scales dst+8 by k when a byte flag is zero, otherwise runs two helper calls with DATA0+64 and DATA0 offsets and scales the same field between them.

guards a fixed data block on an enable byte, takes one of two early exits (setting a pending word and a flag, or skipping), calls two leaves with a scaled value when a byte field matches a threshold word, then clears a byte pair of the block

copies two 16-byte records into locals; when the float threshold is positive it passes the difference of their third components through a float leaf returning the absolute value and, if that is below the threshold, calls one leaf with both records, otherwise the shared alternative leaf
walks 26 consecutive 72-byte records calling one leaf per record, then calls four more leaves on fixed offsets of the same object and returns the object pointer
calls two one-argument functions on a sequence of sub-objects of the argument (four at 8..236 stride 76, nine at 312..888 stride 72) and returns the argument

calls a three-argument helper on the sub-objects at +16 and +32, then packs ((v[6]*v[4])/v[5])<<24 into the low 24 bits of the word at +4 and conditionally calls a second helper on +48 before a final call.
calls one four-argument helper four times, left[i] and right[i] with the float scale, storing each result into dst[i]; the first pointer parameter is unused.

Two size-driven clear loops over one buffer: calls two helpers with a fixed id to obtain a base and an offset, clears 80 records of 112 bytes walking backwards, then clears three fields at offsets 80/84/88 of every 96-byte record up to the buffer end.

Re-initialises a state block: clears field 68, builds two sub-records from the flag word at field 52 masked with 0x200, substitutes a default record for any that came back zero, then clears field 92, sets fields 84 and 80 to -1 and returns 0.
Eased scalar interpolation between a and b: returns a for t==0.0, b for t==1.0, otherwise a + (b-a)*((1-cos(t*pi))*0.5).
Tests the halfword at offset 10 through a helper; on zero it stores a scaled int at offset 4 and a 210000.0f-scaled interpolation of two floats at offset 12, otherwise calls a second helper.
Writes three floats built from two one-float helpers and the three incoming floats: f(b)*a*f(c), g(b)*a*f(c) and g(c)*a.
Loops n times over a 16-byte-strided pointer, scaling the first pointer float at offset 44 by 1/1024 and calling three helpers with that pointer and two offsets of the first argument.
Copies an int argument into a 64-byte stack local, scales the float at offset 44 of the first pointer by 1/1024, and runs five helpers over the two pointers and that local buffer.
Nested 3x3 sweep over two rows-of-four arrays: sums the results of calling the same routine with the difference of each of the nine element pairs, returns the sum.

Fills a three-float record from two helper results scaled by a factor and a third float argument, then runs a setup routine on the record with a bound data root and, when the flag argument is non-zero, a second routine with that root plus 128.
Scales four float arguments by 255, converts each through the same routine, masks each result to a byte and packs the four bytes into one word, low byte first.
Reads one scalar and two helper results, then stores three products of helper pairs each scaled by the scalar into the three floats of the output buffer.

Builds a 3-component vector from a spherical radius/elevation/azimuth triple using two unary float helpers, clears the 4th component, then forwards the destination twice plus a third argument to a final helper.

Builds a 4-float value from a unit seed and a 0.5f-scaled blend against a region 32 bytes into the first argument, squares a scalar returned by a fourth callee, stores the negated complement of that square into a fifth word, converts the value into a 48-byte record and copies that record into the third argument when it is non-null.

Accumulates one float field into another, hands the shortfall to a first callee, scales a forwarded threshold by 0.01f and, when the second callee's result falls below it, snaps the accumulator back and zeroes the threshold holder, returning a float either way.

Fills a two-float scratch buffer from one region of a fixed global, passes it with three forwarded floats and an out-parameter to another callee, stores the returned float back into the global, then feeds that out value to a final callee.
Picks a float threshold (1.0 or 8.0) from a callee status code, compares a probed float against it, and returns a boolean that also latches a trailing probe.

Branches on a float argument: when it is positive it rewrites a float in place with a helper result and sets a field at offset 24 to (helper2 * scale) + offset; otherwise it subtracts a float through a third pointer, rewrites that pointer with (helper2 * scale) and adds it back to the field.

Takes three floats, computes a value from the second and first, negates the third when that value is not positive, clamps the third against that value and its negation (recomputing it in each branch), then calls a helper with the first and the clamped third.

Zeroes six word fields of an object, reads back the first one as a float, calls a helper twice with that float (then with 1.0f) over five float arguments, sets two more int fields, and calls a second helper with two float arguments.

Reads a byte state from a global root; when zero it copies a 16-byte vector and adds a float to its third element, otherwise (state 1 or 2) it builds a 4x4 matrix from a global object and transforms a vector by it.

reads a scalar through DATA0 and, when it exceeds 0.001f, re-normalises the vector at DATA0 (and DATA0-112) from the elapsed float, clamping the amount at zero; otherwise it runs the plain refresh entry point.

reads a base pointer from a0+112 and pushes three consecutive tweak slots through the same five-float interpolation helper, writing each result back over the first float vector while forwarding three trailing floats unchanged.

converts a normalised phase to radians, derives a blend factor of half the complement of a phase helper's result, and applies it to a two-argument helper over three consecutive float components written back over the first vector.

Per frame: scales the value one helper returns by the factor another helper returns, stores both scaled samples and a third sample into a three-float record, and hands the record to a setter with two selector results.

Keeps the float one helper returns, and when a later helper reports a ratio above 0.7 scales it by a factor with a floor, hands it to a setter through a local, then reports whether the kept value is non-zero.

reads a 16-bit state word out of a fixed global block and, when it is non-zero, maps a second byte of that block onto a return code 0/1/2/3; otherwise it runs a reset call, builds a float either from a query on a sub-object of the block or from two floats stored in the block, and classifies it against a stored angle

divides one helper result by a second, multiplies a third by the quotient, quantises that product to a byte lane and the half quotient through two more helpers, bumps a byte counter, adds a scaled helper result to a float field, forwards two 16-byte sub-objects to three helpers, stores the merged byte lanes over a low halfword and calls a trailing helper when a probe on the parameter returns non-zero

scales a float field by 1/1024, passes a caller word and two 16/48-byte scratch buffers to a four-argument helper, then forwards the second buffer with the scaled float to one helper and two sub-objects of the same parameter to three more helpers

decays a float field by 0.04 with a saturating early-out that consults a helper and returns; otherwise adds 12000 to a second field, nudges a third by 0.0484 while it stays below 0.225, merges two 255-scaled byte lanes into a header word, hands a sub-object to two helpers and decrements a byte counter

three-way branch on two 32-bit engine flags: one arm calls a helper, one arm calls a three-argument helper, and the third reads a float from a bound table to pick a +1/-1 scale and issues two helper calls; a final call runs only when the third argument is zero.

branches on a 32-bit field to select a two-byte table entry and a variant of a five-argument call, then converts a scaled field to float and issues a five-float/three-int call with per-branch constants; shared tail call, returns 2.
scales a float field by 1/1024, fills a 64-byte stack buffer from the object, then applies three per-element helper calls over n 64-byte records.
Initialises a record of four 1.0 floats, one zero, one small constant and four zero words, then runs the same four-argument setup four times with two selector flags swept over 0 and 1.
Integrates one float field with a spring-damper step, clamps it to a symmetric limit, then lets a helper raise or lower it, returning a bias plus the field.
Clamps two float fields of one object into [-1,1] through a repeated helper call and copies the clamped values into a second object.
Runs 20 local iterations; the first two calls each pass integer 2 to the same bound target; on each non-null final result, stores a short at +10, an int at +36, and bytes at +42 and +43.
Copies one 16-byte value through the measured helper pipeline and stores the resulting record fields.
